comments.body:
@Fangliding Agreed: this PR does not make the lookup in core faster. It only adds the hook, and without a registered finder nothing changes. Let me explain why the hook is still useful, and what our measurements say about the Linux case above. They may help with the optimization you mentioned.

**Why the hook**

We embed Xray-core as a library in a desktop client for Windows and Linux. The `process` rule is the base of its split tunneling. With the hook, the client registers its own finder at start. Today we carry the hook as a patch.

Our finder against `net.FindProcess`: Xray-core v26.10.31, VMs with 2 vCPUs (Windows 10 22H2, Ubuntu 26.04 as root), 2000 sockets, median of 5 runs:

| Lookup | System | `net.FindProcess` | Registered finder |
|---|---|---|---|
| New TCP connection | Linux | 7.7 ms | 11.5 µs |
| New TCP connection | Windows | 1.97 ms | 0.94 ms |
| Existing connection | Linux | 7.6 ms | 4.1 µs |
| Existing connection | Windows | 1.98 ms | 3.4 µs |

**Where the time goes on Linux**

The socket table is the cheap part. The cost is the step from the socket inode to the PID: a `readlink` of each `/proc/<pid>/fd/*`. In our benchmarks, each descriptor adds about 1.5 to 2 µs. This fits the report above: about 223k descriptors × 2 µs ≈ 0.45 s for each new connection.

This is probably also why netlink did not win for you. `sock_diag` gives the inode fast, but it replaces only the cheap part. Our first finder used `sock_diag` and a cache inode → PID, but it still read all descriptors of the process for each new socket. With 2000 sockets it needed 3.5 ms: only about 2 times faster than core. The large gain came from reading fewer descriptors:

1. A cache inode → PID. An existing connection then needs no `readlink`.
2. The processes of the last found sockets come first.
3. Linux gives a new descriptor the lowest free number. Thus for a recent process, the finder first reads the descriptor numbers of its last found sockets (a closed socket frees its number) and its lowest free numbers. Only if this fails, it reads all descriptors of that process, and then the other processes.

A cache miss still costs a full scan. A new socket of a process that is not recent, or a socket that gets the number of an old closed descriptor, costs about the same as now. We did not measure a desktop with about 223k descriptors, so I cannot give a number for that case.

The idea above, to read `/proc/<pid>/comm` or the `exe` link first and scan only the processes that a rule can match, can remove most of that scan: about 2650 small reads in place of about 223k `readlink` calls. `comm` has at most 15 characters, so a rule with a longer name or with a path needs the `exe` link.

If you improve the lookup in core, the hook is less important for Linux. It still lets an application bring a finder and a cache that fit its platform, as `RegisterAndroidProcessFinder` already does on Android.

With **Kill Switch enabled**, connecting to an AmneziaWG server on Windows never completes: the client stays in "Connecting" (spinner) forever, and at the same time DNS and all Internet access die on **every** adapter — Windows reports "No Internet" while the cable is connected and DHCP keeps working.

Disabling Kill Switch makes the **same server** connect in ~1–2 seconds and everything works. Re-enabling Kill Switch and pressing Connect reproduces the failure every time.

This looks like a bootstrap deadlock:

- the Kill Switch WFP rules permit traffic only through the VPN interface (and appear to whitelist `AmneziaVPN.exe`);
- the WireGuard/AmneziaWG handshake is performed by the client **service** `AmneziaVPN-service.exe` (`tunneldaemon`, service `AmneziaWGTunnel$AmneziaVPN`) over the **physical** adapter to the server endpoint;
- those handshake packets are blocked, so the tunnel never comes up;
- meanwhile the blocking rules are already active, so DNS/Internet is dead on all adapters.

The state is only cleared by Disconnect (or, in an earlier failure, by a reboot) — consistent with stale WFP filters (cf. #3198).

issues.title: Blocking of AmneziaVPN by mobile carriers in strict-DPI jurisdictions (RU/IR/CN, etc.) + a working fix and a request for per-client access management
issues.body:
Body:

Problem:

Users connecting through mobile carriers in countries with active DPI (Russia, Iran, China, etc.) experience blocking or dropped connections on high UDP ports (30000+). The same users on wired/Wi-Fi connections see no difference between ports - so the issue is tied specifically to the mobile channel, not to the protocol itself.

A fix we found and use:

We worked around this on our own infrastructure by moving the service to port 443/udp instead of the default high port. This fully resolves the connection issue even under the harshest network conditions.

But this fix comes at a cost: it requires manual server configuration (changing the port, along with related firewall/network rule adjustments) - meaning it's out of reach for a typical user, and it removes the main advantage that makes AmneziaVPN valuable in the first place: simple, one-click setup. Right now this fix is only available to those willing to administer a server themselves.

So we'd suggest: make port 443/udp the default (or at least a suggested option with a clear explanation, e.g. "for restrictive networks") right in the setup wizard - so an average user gets a working connection without touching the console.

A second, related issue - access management in a small group:

In practice we've found another gap: the client is clearly designed for a "one person, several of their own devices" scenario, but it's also used to distribute access to a small group of people managed by one administrator. Two things get in the way here:

The name entered in the "New user" field doesn't make it into the vpn:// link itself - the user only sees the server's name/description, not their own profile name.
There's no way to revoke access for a single person - for example, in case of a violation of the hosting provider's terms of use (in the EU jurisdiction this includes requirements to comply with copyright and other legal restrictions). Instead, configs have to be reissued for the entire group. For an administrator who is responsible to the hoster for compliance with these terms, the lack of per-client revocation isn't just an inconvenience - it's a real risk to the whole service.

It would be great to get both of these improvements - along with the simplified default for restrictive networks mentioned above.

We're happy to share more details about our approach to working around the blocking, if that would be useful to the project.

issues.title: [Android 14–16] Oneway Binder ~512 KB overflow on large splitTunnelSites in VPN_CONFIG Intent + bitwise `and` bug in AmneziaActivity.kt:437
issues.body:
## Summary
On Android 16 (`arm64`, AmneziaVPN `v5.1.1.10` commit `c71e65d`), importing a full regional CIDR split-tunneling exclusion list (e.g. ~12,800 IPv4 CIDRs in `VpnAllExceptSites` / route mode 2, ~235 KB JSON -> ~515–540 KB UTF-16 `Parcel`) causes deterministic VPN service startup failure across AWG2, WireGuard, and Xray, even though the UI import itself succeeds without crashing.

Log forensics revealed **three coupled defects** in the Android IPC and Foreground Service startup path:

### Defect 1 (Critical IPC): Full `vpnConfig` (with `splitTunnelSites`) sent over oneway Binder (`~512 KB` cap)
- `VpnConnection::appendSplitTunnelingConfig()` (`client/vpnConnection.cpp`) embeds the entire `splitTunnelSites` array into `vpnConfig` JSON, which `AmneziaActivity.startVpnService()` and `connectToVpn()` pass via `Intent.putExtra("VPN_CONFIG", vpnConfig)` and `Messenger.send`.
- A ~520 KB UTF-16 Parcel fits under the ~1 MB synchronous Binder limit (`Activity -> system_server`), so `AmneziaActivity` does not crash. However, `ActiveServices.sendServiceArgsLocked()` (`scheduleServiceArgs`) dispatches `onStartCommand` to `:amneziaAwgService` / `:amneziaXrayService` over an **asynchronous (`oneway`) Binder transaction**, which the kernel caps at `free_async_space` (~512 KB = 520,192 bytes).
- **Cold start:** child process runs `AmneziaApplication.onCreate()` and dies in 13–20 ms before `AmneziaVpnService.onCreate()`, surfacing `Binding to the org.amnezia.vpn/... unexpectedly died`.
- **Proposed fix:** Write `active_vpn_config.json` atomically into `Context.filesDir` (or pass via `ParcelFileDescriptor` / `ashmem`) and send only the file path + config generation ID in the `Intent` / `Messenger` bundle.

### Defect 2 (Bitwise bug in `AmneziaActivity.kt:437`)
- `bindService(it, serviceConnection, BIND_ABOVE_CLIENT and BIND_AUTO_CREATE)` uses Kotlin bitwise `and` (`0x08 & 0x01 == 0`) instead of `or` (`0x08 | 0x01 == 0x09`), passing `0` flags to `bindService`.

### Defect 3 (Android 14–16 ForegroundService timeout in `AmneziaVpnService.kt`)
- When the service process is already warm (e.g. triggered by system Always-on VPN with empty `LAST_CONF`), `onCreate()` and `onBind()` succeed, `scheduleServiceArgs` drops the oversized `onStartCommand` Parcel, `ServiceCompat.startForeground()` is never reached, and Android 16 kills the process after `30.016 s` with `ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException`.
- **Proposed fix:** Call `ServiceCompat.startForeground()` immediately upon entering `onStartCommand()` (before heavy config parsing) and call `stopSelf()` cleanly after `startForeground()` if `LAST_CONF` is empty/invalid.

## Related Issues & PRs
- #2064 (Android 16 split tunneling failure)
- #2735 (Large split-tunneling list startup degradation)
- #2937 / #2939 (`IpSplitTunnelingController` CIDR handling)
- #3262 (`app.log` vs `tunnel.log` live tail behavior when service dies pre-fork)
- #3379, #3405, #3409 (Split tunneling route modes & `:amnezia*Service` crash-loop handling)

issues.title: fix(xray): move saved REALITY configs off the hellochrome_120 fingerprint
issues.body:
Fixes #3413

## Problem

A new self-hosted XRay (VLESS + REALITY) server installed by the app does not pass traffic. The client shows "Connected", but every connection ends on the decoy site instead of going through the server.

## Root cause

- The client default fingerprint is `hellochrome_120` ([protocolConstants.h#L72](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/ac175c8a8147cfe56f98c8372ec17ea2ba00bb02/client/core/utils/constants/protocolConstants.h#L72)).
- The server image installs Xray v26.10.31 ([Dockerfile#L4](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/ac175c8a8147cfe56f98c8372ec17ea2ba00bb02/client/server_scripts/xray/Dockerfile#L4)). That release uses REALITY `83f621788ca8`, which contains XTLS/REALITY@8cdf7bf9c7f09cb9814bf08c3eb877f68b85fba8: a ClientHello without an `X25519MLKEM768` key share (placed before the optional `X25519` one) is no longer authenticated and is forwarded to the target as an ordinary visitor ([tls.go#L215-L236](https://github.com/XTLS/REALITY/blob/83f621788ca88b83179810b12baa7ae518aacb83/tls.go#L215-L236)).
- uTLS `HelloChrome_120` has no `X25519MLKEM768` share, so the server treats the client as a probe. The client then gets the target's real certificate, REALITY verification fails on every connection, and the Xray process itself keeps running, so the app still reports "Connected".
- The same check rejects several entries of the REALITY fingerprint list ([xrayConfigModel.cpp#L760-L763](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/ac175c8a8147cfe56f98c8372ec17ea2ba00bb02/client/ui/models/protocols/xrayConfigModel.cpp#L760-L763)): `ios`, `android`, `edge`, `360`, `qq`, and `random` most of the time (it picks one of Xray's "modern" presets at start, several of which are older Chrome/iOS/Edge hellos).
- Configs created while `hellochrome_120` was the default keep it: in the stored server settings (`xray_fingerprint`), in the saved client config, and in keys/links exported from them.

## Fix

- Update after #3458: `dev` now defaults to `firefox`, which also sends `X25519MLKEM768`, so this PR no longer changes the default. New configs are fine; what remains is the REALITY-only list and moving configs saved with the old default (below). The branch is merged with the current `dev`.
- The REALITY dropdown uses a new `realityFingerprintOptions()` = `chrome`, `firefox`, `safari`: the presets the bundled server accepts. The TLS dropdown keeps the full `fingerprintOptions()` list, because a plain TLS inbound accepts any ClientHello.
- Saved configs that still carry the old default are moved to the new one, for REALITY only:
  - `XrayServerConfig::fromJson()` replaces `hellochrome_120` with the default unless the security is `tls`, so the settings page and new exports use a working value;
  - `sanitizeNativeConfig()`, which already repairs the legacy `Mozilla/5.0` value on every connect (desktop and mobile), also replaces `hellochrome_120` in `realitySettings`. This fixes already issued `vpn://` keys on the receiving side without re-sharing.

  `hellochrome_120` cannot complete a REALITY handshake with any Xray server that has 8cdf7bf, while the default works with both old and new servers (it also sends a plain `X25519` share), so the replacement cannot break a working connection. Other values a user picked on purpose (including `ios`, `edge` and so on) are left as they are; TLS settings are not touched.

## How tested

Sandboxed Linux containers, no network except loopback.

1. Real Xray handshake. Server: official Xray v26.10.31 (the version from the Dockerfile) with VLESS + REALITY + vision. Client: official Xray v26.7.28, which is what amnezia-xray-bindings 1.5.0 wraps (amnezia-xray-core v1.260728.0 has the same `transport/internet/tls/tls.go`, REALITY client and uTLS version). issues.title: [macOS] After GUI crash, stale root-owned tun2socks keeps utun; all reconnects fail with ErrorCode 804 until service restart
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When the AmneziaVPN GUI crashes (or is otherwise relaunched while a session is up), the root-owned `tun2socks` process started by `AmneziaVPN-service` keeps running and keeps holding the `utun` interface and the previous local SOCKS port. The relaunched GUI then cannot recover on its own:

- every connect attempt logs `Tun2socks process was closed with 1 exit code` followed by `Failed to terminate tun2socks. Killing the process...`
- the UI then shows **ErrorCode::804 (Internal error)** on each attempt
- the stale `tun2socks` is never actually killed (it is root-owned; the GUI's terminate/kill does not affect it), and the Xray core's local SOCKS port is no longer listening, so even the surviving tunnel interface carries no traffic

Only a full manual recovery helps: quit the GUI, `killall tun2socks` as root, and `launchctl kickstart -k system/AmneziaVPN-service`. After that, connecting works again.

### To Reproduce

1. Connect to a VLESS server (Amnezia Premium) on macOS.
2. Have the GUI process die while connected (in our case it crashed with the stack-overflow crash from #3497; force-quitting the GUI may work the same way).
3. Relaunch AmneziaVPN and press Connect.
4. Observe ErrorCode 804 on every attempt; `ps` shows the old `tun2socks` (root) still alive; the GUI logs `Failed to terminate tun2socks`.

### Expected behavior

On startup (or on connect), the client should detect and clean up leftover `tun2socks` instances and stale utun interfaces — e.g. via the privileged service, which owns those processes — instead of failing with a generic internal error until a manual service restart.

### Log excerpt (unified log)

```text
E  AmneziaVPN (QtCore) "Tun2socks process was closed with 1 exit code"
Df AmneziaVPN (QtCore) Failed to terminate tun2socks. Killing the process...
E  AmneziaVPN (QtCore) VpnProtocol error, code ErrorCode::804(Код ошибки: 804. Внутренняя ошибка)
```

(repeats on every connect attempt)

State observed while broken:

```text
root  1804  tun2socks -device tun://utun22 -proxy socks5://...@127.0.0.1:52876   # stale, from before the crash
utun22: inet 10.33.0.2 up, but no listener on 127.0.0.1:52876 (Xray core gone) → no traffic
default route still via en0
```

### Environment

- AmneziaVPN 5.1.1 (build 10), installed from `AmneziaVPN_5.1.1.10_macos_x64.pkg`, native ARM64
- macOS 27.2 (26B123), MacBookPro18,3 (Apple M1 Pro)
- Amnezia Premium, VLESS, site split tunneling (VpnAllExceptSites) enabled

Possibly related: #3146 (tun2socks failure → Error 804 on Windows).

issues.title: [macOS] App hangs on launch (100% CPU, no window, only tray icon) when displays are mirrored
issues.body:
## Description
After updating to 5.1.1.9, the app no longer opens its main window on macOS. Only the tray icon appears and the main thread spins at 100% CPU. Disconnecting the external monitor fixes it immediately — the app launches normally.

## Environment
- AmneziaVPN: 5.1.1 (9), `AmneziaVPN_5.1.1.9_macos_x64.pkg`
- macOS: 14.7.2 Sonoma (23H311)
- Hardware: MacBook Pro M2 (Mac14,7), 8 GB
- Displays (mirror mode):
  - Built-in Retina: 2560×1600 (scale 2×)
  - Samsung Odyssey G91SD: 5120×1440 (32:9, scale 1×) — set as Main

## Steps to reproduce
1. Connect an external monitor with a different aspect ratio/scale factor than the built-in display.
2. Enable display mirroring.
3. Launch AmneziaVPN.

## Expected behavior
Main window opens.

## Actual behavior
- Only the tray icon is shown, the window never appears.
- The `AmneziaVPN` main thread is stuck in a busy loop (~100% CPU) — macOS spindump reports a hang.
- `AmneziaVPN-service` is running normally (idle in its event loop).
- After disconnecting the external monitor, the app starts normally.

## Spindump excerpt
Main thread is spinning at the same address for all 79 samples (7.85s):

    Thread 0x115fe  DispatchQueue "com.apple.main-thread"  79 samples  cpu time 7.770s
      ??? (AmneziaVPN + 2828644) [0x10120a964] 1-79

Full spindump attached.

## Possible cause
Probably a Qt window geometry / devicePixelRatio recalculation loop when the window is restored on a mirrored screen whose scale factor differs between the physical displays (2× vs 1×).

## Workaround
Launch the app before connecting the external monitor, or use extended desktop mode instead of mirroring.

fix(udphop): unblock timeout delivery when closing the connection
issues.body:
When the UDP hop receive queue is full, `recvLoop` can block while forwarding a read timeout. Closing the connection stops the socket but does not unblock that channel send, leaving the receive goroutine alive.

Select between delivering the timeout and `closeChan`, so closing the wrapper also interrupts a pending timeout notification. Normal timeout forwarding is unchanged. Add a regression that fills the queue, observes the timeout read, calls the real `Close`, and requires the receiver to exit; cleanup is bounded on assertion failures.

Validation:

- The regression fails on the original code and passes with this change.
- [Complete fork validation](https://github.com/lanqing431/hysteria/actions/runs/46025651571) passed on Linux with Go 1.26.11: the upstream format check and full `core`, `extras`, and `app` test commands, with the Python helpers installed and activated.
- Additional UDP hop race tests passed: `go test -race -count=10 -timeout=3m ./transport/udphop`.

The validation branch contains an additional manual workflow; this PR changes only the UDP hop implementation and its regression test. This is a source-discovered defect, with no unrelated issue closure.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex performed the investigation, implementation, review, and validation under the account owner's authorization.

issues.title: 修复 direct outbound UDP 目标域名每包重复解析
issues.body:
## 问题

direct outbound 转发 UDP 时，若目标是域名（如 `www.gstatic.com:443`），每个包都会重新解析。DNS 返回顺序轮换时，同一条 QUIC 流会被发往多个 IP，引发握手重传或超时。

关联 issue：https://github.com/HyNetworks/hysteria/issues/1725 （报告者已将其改标题为 Withdrawn 并关闭；本报告只针对当前源码中仍可复现的行为。）

## 根因与改动

- 管道中的 resolver 只在 `UDP(reqAddr)` 建会话时填充 `AddrEx.ResolveInfo`；`udpConnAdapter.WriteTo` 每包新建 `AddrEx`，`ResolveInfo` 恒为 nil。
- `directOutboundUDPConn.WriteTo` 原先只缓存 IP 字面量，域名每包调用 `net.LookupIP`，并且绕过了配置中的 resolver。
- 现在同一 UDP 会话内对同一 `host:port` 只解析一次并复用缓存的 `AddrPort`；`UDP()` 建会话时 resolver 已给出的 `ResolveInfo` 直接作为缓存初值；慢路径加锁，保证并发首包只解析一次。IP 字面量路径、以及调用方显式传入 `ResolveInfo` 的行为保持不变。缓存为会话级，未引入 TTL。

## 验证

- 环境：Windows 11 x64，Go 1.27.4（`C:\Program Files\Go\bin\go.exe`），base `7040c16`。
- 新增 4 个针对性单测（注入计数 resolver）：域名连续 3 包只解析 1 次；并发 10 包只解析 1 次；IP 字面量 0 次解析；复用 `UDP()` 阶段的 resolver 结果。
- 回退证明：保留新测试、仅回退实现后 3 个测试失败（解析次数实际为 3 / 10，期望 1；复用解析器结果时报 packet-time resolve 错误），IP 字面量对照仍通过；恢复实现后 4/4 通过。
- `go test ./outbounds/...`（GOWORK=off，extras 模块）通过；唯一失败为 `tinydoh/TestResolver`，它访问外部 `https://1.1.1.1/dns-query`，本机返回 Bad Gateway，该包未被本次改动触及。
- `core` 模块 `go test ./...` 全部通过。
- `gofmt` 已执行；`git diff --check` 无问题。

## 未验证 / 限制

- `app` 模块 `go test ./...` 失败：`internal/utils/certloader_test.go` 缺少 `./testcerts/cert` 等生成的证书文件，属仓库 fixture 缺失，与本次改动无关。
- `-race` 未能运行：本机 CGO 链接器（旧 MinGW）缺少 `WaitOnAddress` 等符号；并发行为由确定性计数测试覆盖。
- 未做真实网络抓包或真实 QUIC 流验证（按要求未启动网络服务）。
- 会话级缓存不做 TTL 刷新：长连接期间 DNS 变更不会生效，符合本问题对“同一条流稳定”的诉求。

Refs: https://github.com/HyNetworks/hysteria/issues/1725

security: harden ACL matching, authenticators, masquerade and log handling
issues.body:
## Problem

- ACL rules are normalized to lower case but matched against the raw host name, so upper-case names bypass domain and geosite rules; the wildcard matcher also backtracks exponentially.
- The password and user/password authenticators compare secrets with plain string equality, and the latter short-circuits on unknown users, revealing whether a user exists.
- The HTTP authenticator reads the backend response without a size limit.
- The masquerade HTTP/HTTPS servers have no read or idle timeouts, and the HTTPS redirect is built from the unvalidated Host header.
- The masquerade file server follows symlinks, so a link inside the served directory exposes files outside it.
- The local SOCKS5 UDP relay treats the first datagram from any source as the client, so a third party can claim the association.
- The HTTP proxy lets the Host header override the request-URI authority.
- The traffic stats endpoint is unauthenticated when the secret is empty, exposing connection destinations.
- Destination addresses are written at warning level, and the server returns raw dial errors that contain the host name and the resolver address.
- TLS verification can be disabled without a pin or CA, and the key exchange does not prefer a post-quantum group.

## Solution

- Normalize the host before ACL matching and replace the recursive wildcard matcher with a linear one.
- Use constant-time secret comparison in both authenticators and drop the early exit that reveals user existence.
- Bound the size of the auth backend response.
- Add header, read and idle timeouts to the masquerade servers, and validate the redirect host.
- Resolve the masquerade root once and reject any path that escapes it through symlinks.
- Tie the UDP association to the source address of the TCP control connection.
- Prefer the request-URI authority over the Host header.
- Require a secret for non-loopback traffic stats listeners, allow an empty secret only for loopback callers, and compare it in constant time.
- Keep destinations at debug level and return a generic message instead of the raw dial error.
- Refuse to disable TLS verification unless a pin or CA is configured (or an explicit environment opt-in is set), and prefer X25519MLKEM768.
- Pad authentication and TCP handshake payloads to fixed sizes so their length does not depend on the secret or host name length.

Verified against a local server/client pair, including an on-path relay capturing the wire traffic.

issues.title: fix(server): reset unexpected streams instead of closing the connection
issues.body:
After auth, `ProxyStreamHijacker` passes any stream that does not start with a TCP request frame back to HTTP/3. If that stream starts with something other than HEADERS, HTTP/3 closes the whole QUIC connection with `H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED`, and every proxied stream on it drops.

I see this from Shadowrocket clients on iOS/macOS. My server logged about 40 `accepting stream failed: H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED (local): expected first frame to be a HEADERS frame` disconnects in 3 hours, each one killing open SSH sessions.

This change:
- lets HEADERS streams through to HTTP/3 as before
- returns an error for other unknown frame types, so http3 resets only that stream and the connection stays up
- reads `authenticated` under `authMutex`, because `ServeHTTP` sets it from another goroutine

`TestServerUnexpectedStreamAfterAuth` fails on master with `Application error 0x105 (remote)` and passes with the fix. `go test ./...` in `core` passes.
